listenings.text: People always ask where it started, and the honest answer is that I did not choose it. My old man pushed me into a wave when I was eight and I have not stopped since. At first I was terrible. I lost every heat for two years and I nearly quit at twelve. Eventually something clicked, and thanks to a coach who refused to let me leave, I stayed. Looking back, the turning point was not a good result. It was the day I understood that the training was the point and the results were just the weather. There have been ups and downs, obviously. But the journey has been worth it.

We have had three exchange students in this house and every single one of them told their story on the first night, at the dinner table, and every single one of them got braver at about week three. What I always say to them is this: your story is the most interesting thing you own here. Nobody at that school has your story. At first they will ask you where you are from, and you will answer in four words. Eventually somebody will ask you properly, and that is when you should take your time. Looking back at all three of them, the ones who told their story are the ones who made friends.

paras: He caught his first wave at eight, on a board that was too big for him, because his father pushed him into it and did not tell him what was going to happen.

At first it went badly. He joined the club at nine and he lost every heat he entered for two years. He finished last in his first competition at twelve and he cried in the car. His coach told him one thing that week: nothing happens in the first two years. He decided to believe it.

Eventually it clicked. At fourteen he stood on the podium for the first time, and thanks to that result the club put him in the junior squad. Looking back, he says the turning point was not the podium. It was the four bad seasons before it, because that is where the training habit came from.

There have been ups and downs since. A shoulder injury took six weeks last year, and he admits that he went back too early and lost another month. He is not proud of the results; he is proud of the fact that he has not missed a Saturday since he was nine.

In February the journey moves to another coast, another school and another language. He has been studying English three times a week since August for exactly that reason. And the story he will tell there starts the same way: my father pushed me into a wave when I was eight.

gist.prompt: Which title fits the text best?
choices: How to win your first junior competition
One journey, told properly: where it started, what changed, where it is going
